summary.headline: Motilal Oswal Q2FY27 operating PAT rose 29% YoY to ₹718 crore, led by Asset & Private Wealth, which grew 43% YoY.
summary.overview: Operating PAT grew 29% YoY to ₹718 crore, with Asset & Private Wealth Management up 43% and now contributing about 58% of operating PAT. AUM for Asset Management plus MO Alternates reached ₹2.23 lakh crore, and PWM AUM reached ₹2.96 lakh crore (up 58% YoY). Management said broking headwinds from regulation and flat markets are in the base and that H2FY27 growth should be higher. The company received a SEBI custodian licence in Q2 and plans to launch the custody business in Q4FY27, with no material contribution expected in FY28.

financial_highlights.metric: Asset & Private Wealth Management PAT growth
financial_highlights.change: Contributes ~58% of operating PAT vs 49% in FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Asset Management share of group operating PAT

financial_highlights.change: Net flows +65% QoQ to ₹6,357 crore; PWM PAT +2% YoY

segments.name: Asset & Private Wealth Management
segments.commentary: Net flows ₹12,477 crore in the quarter; AUM ₹5.2 lakh crore, up 42% YoY. Management expects operating leverage from rising AUM to drive profit growth.

segments.name: AMC (MF, PMS, AIF)
segments.commentary: Q2 net active flows about ₹3,600 crore, alternatives negative, passive ₹1,600 crore; September net active flows about ₹2,100 crore; SIP flows ₹4,170 crore with 4.4% market share in Sept. Passive AUM above ₹50,000 crore. Average AUM ₹2.01 lakh crore in Q2FY27 vs ₹1.67 lakh crore in Q4FY26.

segments.name: MO Alternates
segments.commentary: Final close of ₹3,000 crore maiden private credit fund in progress, with about 90% raised per management. Maiden commercial real estate fund launched in Q2.

segments.name: Wealth Management (broking, distribution, lending)
segments.commentary: Overall retail broking market share including commodity 7.9% in Q2FY27; F&O premium share 7.6% to 8.8% and cash share 6.8% to 8.0% QoQ. MTF market share about 7%.

segments.name: Capital Markets (IB and Institutional Equities)
segments.commentary: 41 deals in H1FY27 with cumulative raise of ₹99,000 crore; ranked #1 in QIP and #3 in IPO in H1FY27. Research coverage above 400 companies, targeting 500.

segments.name: Housing Finance
segments.commentary: AUM ₹6,476 crore (+24% YoY); management guides GNPA normalising to 1.1%-1.2%, with 1+, 30+ and 90+ delinquency pools all lower YoY.

guidance_outlook: Management targets sustainable 20% profit CAGR and 20%+ ROE; decadal operating profit CAGR of 33%, EPS CAGR 26%, average ROE 23%.
H2FY27 growth expected to be higher than H1FY27, with PWM PAT growth expected to be much higher in H2 than H1.
Custody business to launch in Q4FY27 subject to operational readiness; no material contribution even in FY28; product positioning guidance after at least three quarters.
SIF launch expected around Q4FY27; a next alternates product series expected in calendar 2027.
Expects the commercial real estate fund to close within about 6 months.
Expects broking market share to improve and commodity market share to recover quickly.
capex_capacity: SEBI custodian of securities licence received in Q2FY27; CEO and senior team hired, operations to start Q4FY27.
PWM hiring: 443 RMs, about one-third with 3+ years vintage; hiring now more judicious, with additions in ultra-HNI segment.
AMC: 24 schemes above ₹1,000 crore vs 16 a year earlier; only 6 funds over 3 years old, rising to 8 by Mar-27 and 16 by Mar-28.
Housing Finance: management says growth of similar magnitude expected over 2-3 years with high capital adequacy and low leverage, no external equity needed.
Treasury book about 98% equity: 55% AMC funds, 16% Alternates funds, 29% direct equity.
demand_pricing: AMC: management says performance is the main driver of inflows; funds delivered about 6% alpha last quarter; 99% of AUM outperforming benchmark on 3-year basis.
Small cap is the largest inflow category; large and mid cap second. Small cap crosses 3-year vintage in December, followed by large cap and multi-cap over the following 3 months.

Lending: MTF book growth is in line with market; ex-HFC lending book about ₹17,500 crore, of which MTF about ₹9,600 crore, T+5 and bank guarantee financing about ₹4,800 crore, and loan against shares about ₹3,100 crore.
Commodity ADTO share fell as discount brokers scaled commodity divisions; management expects quick recovery.
PWM new-customer flows about 20% of net flows; most flows come from existing customers.

qa_highlights.question: How will custody business scale over two years, and is it ARR accretive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to comment; launch targeted Q4FY27, product offering still being formulated, and no material contribution even in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What are PWM RM hiring plans and breakeven profile?
qa_highlights.answer: About one-third of RMs have under one year vintage and have not yet broken even; RMs typically break even within a year and are profitable within 2-3 years. Hiring continues more selectively, mainly in ultra-HNI.

qa_highlights.question: Why did market share in cash and F&O pick up sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash share gain was driven by MTF book growth in line with market; F&O options share gained as the company advised cautious options trading and performed better when volumes were lower. Futures outperformed the market.

qa_highlights.question: Why did AMC net flows moderate, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 flows were a little higher than Q1 after 2-3 lean months; September net active flows were about ₹2,100 crore and October expected over ₹2,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How much VAR was booked and how will carry income evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: VAR booked was ₹106 crore, currently accruing largely from two mature schemes; it is expected to grow as funds approach exit and each series raises about 2x the prior AUM.

qa_highlights.question: What is the insurance revenue mix and asset quality outlook in housing finance?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance is about 3% of Wealth Management operating revenue and about 7% of housing finance revenue. Management expects GNPA to normalise to 1.1%-1.2%, with H2FY27 asset quality improving.

risks_watch: Custody business launch timing and economics remain undefined; no material FY28 contribution expected.
Broking revenue headwinds from regulatory changes and flat markets over the last 8 quarters; management says these are in the base.
Lending growth (MTF and loan book) is fast-growing; customer quality and mix were questioned in Q&A.
Potential impact of a proposed consultation paper on insurance revenue was raised but not quantified.
Housing finance H1 seasonality in delinquencies; management targets GNPA normalisation to 1.1%-1.2%.
Alternates private credit final close (₹3,000 crore) still pending; management held back about 10% of the pipeline awaiting domestic institutional flows.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the Asset & PWM growth trajectory and the outlook for H2FY27, while cautious and noncommittal on the custody business, which it said is too early to quantify. Management was direct on AMC flow recovery and gave specific figures on VAR and lending mix.
key_quotes: We believe the regulatory headwinds are in the base and the continued resilience displayed by Indian investors, future outlook for capital market player like us to deliver sustainable 20% Profit CAGR with 20%+ ROE is likely.
Very tough to comment anything as of now. We are hoping to launch this business in the Q4FY27.
The trend has definitely come back to how it used to be earlier. Performance is a biggest driver for inflows.
